summary: Independent read of the device hash map S2 review fixes (writer slots, dead-writer discount, liveness, claim and its start-time record), each finding checked by a refuter

findings.title: Pass 1 takes a slot by CAS on the owner word and stores the start time afterwards. A second claimant then steals a live process's slot, its in-flight writer is discounted, and the seal returns true while that writer still writes the table
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:316-337 (pass 1: cpp:322-330 reads start after owner; CAS cpp:331; start store cpp:335), 355-381 (discount), 411 (fetch_sub wraps); compare the OWNER fix 0b9b02af, cpp:468-474 and 487-491
findings.problem:
The 0b9b02af fix (a start time counts only when it was written for the current record) covers OWNER only. Writer slots still have the same window.

When pass 1 takes a dead process's slot, the CAS changes owner from D to X while start still holds D's start time S_D. X's own start S_X is stored one instruction later. During that window another process Y in pass 1 reads owner X, count 0 and start S_D. devhash_process_alive(X, S_D) sees the start-time mismatch, treats live X as a reused pid, and Y's CAS X->Y succeeds.

X then stores S_X over Y's start and returns the same slot. The slot now reads {owner Y, start S_X}, and both processes' first updates count in it. Since Y's start differs from S_X, discount_dead_writers judges Y gone and stores count 0 while a writer that read PHASE 0 is in the table. The seal returns true and the image misses that write.

The writer's fetch_sub then leaves count = 2^64-1 in a slot with owner 0. Pass 0 gives that slot to the next writer process. Sums are wrapping u64, so that writer's +1 cancels the -1, and later seals also return true with that writer in flight. This lasts until the slot's next owner dies.

Precondition: pass 1 runs only when no slot has owner 0. Only a seal's discount frees a slot. A process that exits with count 0 keeps its slot until a pass-1 claimant takes it. So once 64 writer processes have claimed slots in a segment, every new process's first update takes pass 1. Every newcomer scans from index 0, so concurrent newcomers compete for the same first dead slot. A preemption in the two-instruction window is needed. It is narrow, but no fault is required.
findings.evidence:
Deterministic reproduction against build-cuda/runtime/libruntime.a, harness /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-s2-reread/slots/h.cpp. Setup: slot 0 = a reaped pid with start 12345, slots 1..63 = a live keeper. X ran under gdb with a breakpoint at my_writer_slot+368 (cpp:335, after __aarch64_cas8_acq_rel). Y ran from gdb's shell while X was stopped. Then X continued and was parked by the writer_after_phase_load hook, and the orchestrator sealed:
```
Breakpoint 1, my_writer_slot ... nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:335
[y 4098400] update returned 0
  [after y] slot 0: owner pid 4098400 start 105409682 count 0
[x 4098397] in flight, read PHASE 0
  [x in flight] slot 0: owner pid 4098400 start 105409651 count 1
[info] device hash map: discounting 1 writer(s) of pid 4098400, which is gone   <- Y is alive
[o] seal_and_build -> 1 (phase 1, seal_dead 0), inflight 0
[o] x returned 0; key 4242 in the image: 0, in the CPU table now: 1
[o] inflight after x finished: 18446744073709551615
  [end] slot 0: owner pid 0 start 0 count -1
```
Follow-on (w.cpp, case 1): a free slot with count ~0 is taken by the next writer's pass 0, and the seal returns true with that writer stopped in flight:
```
(1) writer 4121112 stopped in flight after reading PHASE 0; slot 0 owner pid 4121112 count 0; inflight sum 0
    seal_and_build with that writer in flight: 1; key in image 0; writer exit 0; key in CPU table now 1
```
findings.suggested_change: Make (owner, start) change as one unit. One way, as discount already does with ~0: CAS owner cur -> a CLAIMING sentinel, store start, then store owner = self with release. The first loop, pass 1 and the discount must take the sentinel as taken and alive. Another way: a start_for word, as 0b9b02af did for OWNER, with start counted as unknown (alive) unless it was written for the current record. Add a hook between the CAS and the start store (like claim_after_cas) and a test: fill the 64 slots, park X there, and expect a second process to leave X's slot alone. Also keep a decrement from wrapping into a slot that has been discounted and freed. For example, the discount could CAS the count it read to 0 rather than store 0, so a writer that raced in is noticed.

findings.title: exec of a multi-threaded writer process leaks its writers' counts into a slot that is never discounted while the new image runs (same pid, same start time)
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:146-161 (liveness: kill, tasks, start time), 308-315 (the first loop matches the new image to the old slot), 360-366 (discount skips a live process); PLAN-stage1.md:166 (D8 names exit, not exec)
findings.problem:
D8 handles counts left by threads that an exit kills. execve kills a process's other threads in the same way (de_thread), wherever they are. The process keeps its pid and its start time (stat field 22 is unchanged across exec), so devhash_process_alive keeps answering alive and discount_dead_writers never clears the slot.

The seal then times out and sets SEAL_DEAD, and every later attempt fails at once, for as long as the exec'd program runs, even though nothing writes. A long-lived exec'd service (a wrapper that execs the real server, or a runtime's self re-exec) keeps the map without a device copy for its whole life.

If the agent is loaded again in the new image (LD_PRELOAD inherited), its first update matches the same slot by record and start (cpp:313). It keeps using that slot, so the count never returns to 0 for the pid's whole life.
findings.evidence:
/tmp/claude-2002/devhash-s2-reread/slots/e.cpp: a child runs 4 threads looping elem_update, and after 5 ms its main thread execs /proc/self/exe (an image that opens the segment and does one update). The first round leaked:
```
exec'd image 4121248: update -1, uses slot 0 (count 2 after its update)
slot 0: owner pid 4121248 start 105493629 count 2; /proc start now 105493629, alive 1
seal (300 ms) with the exec'd process alive and nothing writing: 0, seal_dead 1, phase 0
again: 0
[info] discounting 2 writer(s) of pid 4121248, which is gone   (only after the exec'd image exited)
after the exec'd process exited: 1, seal_dead 0
```
With /bin/sleep as the new image the result was the same (count 2, alive 1, the seal failing until sleep exited).
findings.suggested_change: Count writers in a way an exec ends. One way: per thread, keyed by (pid, tid, thread start time from /proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/stat), probed as ringbuf's is_thread_gone does. Another: put a random per-image id in the slot. A new image's first claim may then zero a slot that has its own pid and start but another image id, because no thread of an earlier image survives exec. Otherwise write the exec case into README next to the exit case, and add a test (a writer process that execs while its threads update).

findings.title: A sealer killed between discount's CAS to ~0 and its clearing stores (a log call sits between them) leaves a count no later seal can remove: recover_sealing and every later seal fail for the segment's life
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:370-380 (CAS owner -> ~0 at 370, SPDLOG_INFO at 374-377, count/start/owner stores at 378-380), 359-362 (a later discount skips owner ~0: (~0 >> 32) != self's namespace), 643-650 (recover_sealing); PLAN-stage1.md:330 (D11e: a sealer died)
findings.problem:
discount_dead_writers marks the slot with owner ~0 and then logs through spdlog, which is I/O through the configured sink. Only after the log does it store count 0, start 0 and owner 0.

If the sealer process dies in that window (the CUDA application killed during its attach, OOM), the slot stays {owner ~0, count = the dead writer's leaked count}. Every later discount skips it: the namespace check fails for ~0, so it is neither 'gone' nor reclaimable by pass 1 or pass 0. The sum never reads 0 again.

D11e's path for a dead sealer (PHASE 1 -> recover_sealing) therefore always times out to SEAL_DEAD, and so does every later attempt by any process, until the segment is recreated. Nothing is writing.
findings.evidence:
/tmp/claude-2002/devhash-s2-reread/slots/s.cpp. A writer was killed in flight (slot 0 count 1). A sealer process ran under gdb with a breakpoint at discount_dead_writers+192 (cpp:374, after the successful CAS) and was killed there. Then three attempts from another process:
```
dead writer 4105702 in slot 0: owner pid 4105702 count 1
after the killed sealer: slot 0 owner 0xffffffffffffffff count 1, phase 1, inflight 1
attempt 0 (recover_sealing): 0, seal_dead 1, slot 0 owner 0xffffffffffffffff count 1
attempt 1 (seal_and_build): 0, seal_dead 1, slot 0 owner 0xffffffffffffffff count 1
attempt 2 (seal_and_build): 0, seal_dead 1, slot 0 owner 0xffffffffffffffff count 1
```
findings.suggested_change: Log after the three stores, so the window is two plain stores. Then make it recoverable. Only the process holding the owner claim discounts, so a slot with owner ~0 that the current owner sees was left by a dead sealer. The owner may clear it, count included, and so may recover_sealing. Add a test with a hook between the CAS and the stores and a sealer killed there, followed by recover_sealing.

findings.title: The overflow slot is reached with no live writer at all: dead in-flight slots cannot be reused by writers, foreign-namespace slots are never freed, and one process can hold two slots. One later death there wedges the seal for good
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:316-341 (pass 1 frees only same-namespace slots with count 0; overflow at 341), 355-362 (only a seal's discount frees a slot with a count; never another namespace's); nv_gpu_device_hash_map.hpp:141-143; PLAN-stage1.md:147-150, 182-183
findings.problem:
The plan accepts that a writer dying in the overflow slot wedges the seal (D8, plan:182). It presents the overflow as used only 'when all are taken'. In this code three things make the overflow the steady state in phase 0, with no live writer.

(a) A slot whose process died with a count left (the exit leak the review measured at 2-23 of 40 exits) is freed only by a seal's discount. Pass 1 skips it because its count is not 0. In a long phase 0 (a CPU tool running before any GPU agent attaches) such slots accumulate. After 64 of them, every new writer process shares the overflow slot.

(b) A slot claimed by a process of another pid namespace is never freed by this namespace, even at count 0 after that process exits. Each container process that ever wrote holds a slot until the segment is recreated.

(c) The one-slot-per-process rule is not enforced. A thread that loses a pass-0 CAS goes on to the next free slot instead of re-checking whether its process now has one.

Once the overflow is in use, one exit leak there makes SEAL_DEAD permanent, although no process is alive.
findings.evidence:
/tmp/claude-2002/devhash-s2-reread/slots/o.cpp: 65 writer processes, each killed in flight in phase 0 (no seal in between):
```
65 writer processes died in flight: 64 slots hold a dead count, overflow count 1, inflight 65
seal attempt 0: 0, seal_dead 1, inflight 1 (overflow 1)
seal attempt 1: 0, seal_dead 1, inflight 1 (overflow 1)
seal attempt 2: 0, seal_dead 1, inflight 1 (overflow 1)
```
The 64 dead slots were discounted by the first seal, but the overflow count stays and no process is left. /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-s2-reread/slots/t.cpp: 32 threads making their first update at once took up to 2 slots for one process (`max 2, mean 1.2 over 20 rounds`). Point (b) is from the code (cpp:323 and cpp:360 require the same namespace); not run.
findings.suggested_change: Let pass 1 free a dead same-namespace process's slot whatever its count, as the discount does (CAS owner -> ~0, count 0, then free it). A dead process's count is never needed. After a lost pass-0 CAS, re-run the first loop so a process keeps one slot. Write (b) into the README and decide an answer, for example ageing out foreign slots with count 0. Add a test: 64 processes die in flight, and a 65th writer must get a slot of its own, not the overflow.

findings.title: A process that finds every slot held by live processes runs 64 liveness probes (/proc file opens, allocations) on every update: 1.3 ms per update instead of 0.15 us, in the traced process's probe path, with no caching
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:316-341 (pass 1 calls devhash_process_alive for each same-namespace slot with count 0, every call), 77-122 (opendir/fopen/fread per probe), 400-401 and 418-419 (every elem_update/elem_delete calls my_writer_slot first, phase 2 included)
findings.problem:
my_writer_slot remembers no decision. When no slot matches and none is free, both passes run on every call. Pass 1 calls devhash_process_alive for every same-namespace slot whose count is 0. Each call is kill(), opendir(/proc/<pid>/task) with readdir, fopen/fread of a task's stat, and fopen/fread of /proc/<pid>/stat.

With 64 live writer processes holding slots (a CPU probe in a prefork server with more workers, database backends, and so on), every update from the 65th and later processes costs about 64 x 3 file reads. This happens inside the BPF helper in the traced process, with malloc from fopen/opendir. It never improves, because live processes keep their slots.

In phase 2 the same cost is paid only to return EPERM, because the slot is chosen before PHASE is read.
findings.evidence:
/tmp/claude-2002/devhash-s2-reread/slots/t.cpp (2000 updates each):
```
own slot: 0.15 us per update
64 slots held by a live process (overflow): 1312.67 us per update
```
findings.suggested_change: Cache the overflow decision per process, and try for a slot again only after some time (perf output's overflow shard retries after 10 ms, cached per thread). Keep /proc reads off the per-update path. In phase 2, PHASE is terminal (no path stores 0 or 1 after 2), so a relaxed PHASE check before my_writer_slot can return EPERM without claiming a slot or probing.

findings.title: A dead predecessor with the sealer's own pid is never discounted by that sealer. A slot with start 0 is inherited by a reused pid, and its leaked count is then never discounted
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:360 (skips cur == self on the record alone, no start compare), 313 (the `st == 0 || my_start == 0` wildcard), 155-159 (start 0 = unknown = alive)
findings.problem:
(a) discount_dead_writers skips any slot whose record equals the sealer's (namespace, pid). A process that died with a leaked count and whose pid the sealer now has (pid reuse) is never discounted by that sealer, so its seal times out to SEAL_DEAD. Only a sealer with another pid clears it. The first loop handles the same case correctly, by start time.

(b) A slot whose start reads 0 is matched by any process with the same record. This happens when a claimant died between its pass-0 CAS and its start store, or when a process's own start read failed. A process reusing that pid then uses the slot without storing its start and inherits any count left in it. Liveness with start 0 ignores the start time, so while the new process lives the leaked count is never discounted.
findings.evidence:
/tmp/claude-2002/devhash-s2-reread/slots/w.cpp case 2: slot 0 = {this process's record, start 1, count 1} (devhash_process_alive(self, 1) = 0):
```
    seal by this process: 0, seal_dead 1, slot 0 count 1
[info] device hash map: discounting 1 writer(s) of pid 4121111, which is gone   <- from the forked child's seal
    seal by another process (child 4121113): sealed, slot 0 count 0
```
Part (b) is argued from cpp:313 and cpp:155-159; not reproduced.
findings.suggested_change: In the discount, compare start too. Skip only slots with the sealer's record and its own start or start 0, and treat a slot with its record but another start as a dead predecessor. Do not let a start of 0 match another process: store a start for every claimant, and give a slot whose start is unknown no wildcard match.

findings.title: The start-time cache is two separate static words shared with vfork-style children. A parent thread can pair its pid with the child's start time and claim a slot whose in-flight writers the seal discounts
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:290-304 (current_producer_identity, then static atomics cached_pid and cached_start, stored start-then-pid), 311-314, 335-336
findings.problem:
A vfork or posix_spawn child shares the parent's memory, so it shares these statics too. In syscall-trace mode on aarch64, the identity epoch gives the child its own pid C (CLAUDE.md, producer identity), and the child runs programs, for example on execve's entry.

Interleavings:
- Transient: parent thread T2 loads cached_pid == P. The child then stores cached_start = S_C, before its cached_pid = C. T2 loads S_C.
- Persistent: T2 stores start S_P; a child stores S_C and then C; T2 stores pid P. The cache now reads (P, S_C) for good.

Either way P's writer finds no slot {P, S_P} match. It claims a slot {P, S_C}, and devhash_process_alive(P, S_C) returns false for it. Any seal then discounts P's live writers there, and pass 1 of other processes reclaims that slot.

In Frida mode a vfork or raw-clone child keeps its parent's identity (documented limit), so it counts in the parent's slot. The parent's exit then discounts the child's live writer, and the child's death in flight leaks into a live parent's slot.
findings.suggested_change: Keep (pid, start) in one word, for example pid in the low 22 bits and the start time in ticks above it, or in thread-local storage (a vfork child runs on its parent thread's TLS, but no other thread of the parent can read it then). Get the pid for the slot from getpid() once per image, not from the producer identity, or document the Frida-mode limit for 1533 writers.

verdicts.reason: Holds. Pass 1 at cpp:331-336 does the CAS on owner and stores start afterwards. Between the two, the slot reads {owner X, start = D's start, count 0}, and pass 1's condition at cpp:322-329 treats live X as gone because devhash_process_alive sees the start-time mismatch. 0b9b02af added owner_start_for only for OWNER (cpp:472-474 and 488-491), not for writer slots. The discount at cpp:363-380 then judges live Y gone, because the slot holds X's start, and stores count 0 while X is in flight. X's fetch_sub at cpp:411 wraps the count to 2^64-1. The race is narrow: the window is two instructions and needs a preemption, all 64 slots must have owners, and the pass-1 claimants must be concurrent. No fault is needed, and the result is a wrong image, so blocker fits the rules.

While the wrapped slot is unowned, every seal with no writer in flight fails. I did not rerun the w.cpp follow-on (the next pass-0 writer cancelling the -1), but it follows from the same wrapping sum (bpftime_devhash_sealer_poll, cpp:188-196).

verdicts.reason:
Holds from code reading, and the premise is confirmed. cached_pid and cached_start are two separate function-static atomics (cpp:296-304), which a CLONE_VM child shares. read_identity returns getpid() and does not cache it in a vfork child (producer_identity.cpp:141-155: `pid = getpid(); ... if (pid == process_pid) { cache... }`). Once the epoch is bumped, a vfork child in syscall-trace mode therefore passes its own pid C and stores cached_start = S_C and then cached_pid = C. Two interleavings give the parent (P, S_C):
- Transient: the child's start store lands between a parent thread's two loads.
- Persistent: the stores interleave as start S_P, start S_C, pid C, pid P.
The first loop then fails to match {P, S_P} because both starts are nonzero and differ, so the parent claims {P, S_C}. devhash_process_alive(P, S_C) is false, so a seal discounts P's live writers there. In Frida mode the child keeps the parent's identity, as documented in CLAUDE.md. It needs a probe that updates this map in a vfork child, concurrently with a parent thread's cache refresh. Not reproduced.

findings.title: execve keeps a writer process's pid and start time: counts left by the threads exec killed are never discounted, so no seal succeeds while the exec'd image runs
findings.problem: Setting: a writer process W (a CPU-probed process or tool) has threads inside elem_update/elem_delete. One of W's threads calls execve. Like exit_group, exec kills every other thread wherever it is, so their increments of W's writer slot are never undone. Unlike an exit, W stays alive: same pid, and the same start time (fs/exec.c de_thread copies the leader's start_time/start_boottime to the exec'ing thread). discount_dead_writers frees a slot only when devhash_process_alive(pid, start) is false. For W that is never true while the new image runs, whether or not that image loads the agent. Every seal polls a sum that is never 0. After 1 s it sets SEAL_DEAD, and every later attempt returns at once. The map has no device copy until W exits. D8 covers deaths ('an exit kills its other threads'), but exec is the same thread-killing event with the process kept alive. Precondition: a multi-threaded writer process that execs while threads are in an update. A self re-exec (Go syscall.Exec, a daemon re-exec) is the realistic case.

findings.title: Writer slots run out and are not given back: with 64 live writers each update of a 65th process costs about 1.3 ms in liveness probes, and slots of other pid namespaces are never freed, so all writers end up in the never-discounted overflow slot
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:287-342 (my_writer_slot: pass 0/1 on every call, 322-330 probe, 323 same-namespace only), 355-362 (discount only count != 0, same namespace); PLAN-stage1.md:149-150
findings.problem:
my_writer_slot runs on every elem_update/elem_delete and caches nothing when the process has no slot. A slot is set back to owner 0 only by the sealer's discount, which acts only on slots with count != 0. Slots of dead processes with count 0 stay owned until a new process steals one in pass 1. So once 64 writer processes have existed, no slot is free, and every new process's first write runs pass 1.
(1) Cost: when the 64 slots are held by live writer processes of the same pid namespace (for example a pre-fork server with more than 64 CPU-probed workers), pass 1 calls devhash_process_alive on every slot with count 0 for every update of every further process: kill, opendir/readdir of /proc/<pid>/task, and two stat reads, about 20 us per slot. Then it falls back to the overflow slot.
(2) Permanence: pass 1 (cpp:323) and the discount (cpp:360) consider only slots of their own namespace. Slots of writer processes from namespaces that are gone (container restarts) are never freed by anyone. Neither are slots of processes without /proc, whose namespace id is random per process. With enough of them every writer shares the overflow slot, which is never discounted. One ordinary exit with a thread in flight then sets SEAL_DEAD for the segment's life; concurrency-2 measured 2-23 of 40 exits leaking. The plan says 'a slot of a process that is gone, with nothing in flight, is free again' and documents only that a writer in the overflow slot cannot be discounted, not that foreign slots fill the table for good.

Add a test with 64 live writer processes that bounds the per-update cost.

findings.title: Pass 1 of my_writer_slot stores the start time after the owner CAS: a second process takes the live first one for a reused pid and steals the slot; the discount then zeroes a live writer's count (lost exclusion), and its decrement wraps the sum so no later seal succeeds
findings.problem: This is the window 0b9b02af closed for OWNER, still open for writer slots. P is a live process taking the slot of a dead process D in pass 1. P CASes owner D->P (cpp:331) and only then stores its own start time (cpp:335). Between the two, the slot reads (P's record, D's start, count 0). Q is a second new process in pass 1. Q loads that triple (cpp:318-329): devhash_process_alive(P, D's start) is false because P's start differs, so Q's CAS P->Q succeeds and Q stores its start. P then stores its own start over it. Both use the slot, which now reads (Q, P's start). A seal while either is in that first update discounts it: alive(Q, P's start) is false. The seal returns and the image is built while Q, having read PHASE 0, still writes the CPU table. Q's fetch_sub then takes the count to 2^64-1. That slot is now free (owner 0, cpp:380) and skipped by every discount (cur == 0), so the sum stays wrapped. Every seal times out to SEAL_DEAD until some process takes that slot and later dies. A wrapped slot plus one writer in flight also sums to 0, so a poll can read 0 with a writer inside. Preconditions: no free slot (the normal state after 64 writer processes, owner-2 (A)); Q's loads land in P's two-store window (narrow unless P is preempted there); a seal during one of their first updates.

findings.title: claim() on the same-record path (pid reuse, no cached copy) makes no CAS: a concurrent claimant that pairs the record with the dead predecessor's start time CASes it away, and both take the map
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:466-497 (cur == self skips the CAS at 482; owner_start/owner_start_for stores at 488-491); devhash_choose_path 221-225
findings.problem: R is a record (namespace, pid) whose process D owned the map, recorded start sD and died. P is a new process that got the same pid. P runs claim(R, has_cached_copy=false). cur == self, so devhash_choose_path treats it as pid reuse and returns first_copy, recover_sealing or takeover, and P skips the CAS ('cur != self && !CAS'). P then stores its own start. Meanwhile B is another agent in the same namespace claiming in P's window, from P's owner load to its owner_start store at cpp:488, which includes P's /proc read. B loads owner = R, owner_start_for == R and owner_start = sD, all still D's. devhash_process_alive(P's pid, sD) is false because the start differs, and B's CAS R->B succeeds because OWNER still holds R. P's late stores then set owner_start_for = R while OWNER = B. Both return a copy path. In phase 2 both take over: two device copies and two delivery threads write one mirror, breaking the 'one writer at a time' rule (hpp:37-39), with concurrency-1's wrong values. In phase 0 both seal, and one sealer's timeout path (PHASE 0) can run while the other builds its image.   same-pid claimant path 4 (takeover=4), other claimant path 4, owner==B 1 owner==R 0

For example, take over the dead predecessor's record like any other (CAS R -> 0, then 0 -> R, restarting the loop on failure). findings.title: Liveness reads /proc of the mount's pid namespace and start times shifted by the reader's time namespace: a live owner or writer can be judged dead
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:78-122 (real_tasks_running, real_start_time via /proc/<pid>), 146-161, 301 and 488-489 (own start read through /proc/<getpid()>/stat)
findings.problem: Records hold getpid() of the writer's or owner's own pid namespace, and peers are compared only within one namespace id. kill(pid, 0) works in the caller's namespace. /proc/<pid> resolves in the pid namespace of the /proc mount (proc_pid_lookup uses fs_info->pid_ns). In a process of a new pid namespace with the parent's /proc still mounted (unshare(CLONE_NEWPID) without remounting /proc, as the repo's own namespace test does), several reads hit another process. devhash_process_start_time(getpid()) at claim (cpp:488-489) and in my_writer_slot (cpp:301) records the start of whichever process has that number in the mount's namespace, or 0. real_tasks_running and real_start_time of a peer read that other process too. If that process is a zombie, or exits and its number is reused, a live owner is taken over (two owners) or a live in-flight writer is discounted (lost exclusion plus the wrap of owner-3). Separately, /proc/<pid>/stat field 22 is shifted by the reader's time-namespace boottime offset. An owner or writer recorded in one time namespace and judged from another in the same pid namespace always reads as 'start differs', so it counts as dead. EPERM does not short-circuit to alive (cpp:150-158). Not run here: it needs root or user namespaces, which are blocked on this host (apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1).

- fs/proc/array.c:586-587: 'start_time = nsec_to_clock_t(timens_add_boottime_ns(task->start_boottime));' (the reader's time namespace).
- The configuration exists in this repo: runtime/unit-test/test_software_perf_event.cpp:943 'if (unshare(CLONE_NEWPID) != 0)' then forks pid 1 with no /proc mount, so in that child /proc/1 is the host's init.

Otherwise treat tasks as unknown and start times as 0, which counts as alive. Record the time namespace (inode of /proc/self/ns/time) next to each start time and compare starts only within one time namespace, else treat them as unknown. Document both in D11c.

findings.title: The discount skips every slot with the sealer's own record without comparing start times: after pid reuse, this process can never seal while it lives

D is a writer that died with threads in flight (the common exit leak). If the sealing GPU process G later gets D's pid, D's leftover count is invisible to G's discount: G's seal times out and sets SEAL_DEAD, and each later attempt by G returns at once. Only another process's seal discounts it. If G is the only GPU agent, the map has no device copy for G's lifetime. Precondition: pid reuse of a dead in-flight writer by the sealing process.

findings.title: A sealer killed inside discount_dead_writers leaves the slot as (owner ~0, count > 0), which nothing ever clears: no later seal succeeds
findings.problem: The discount reserves a dead process's slot by CASing owner to ~0 (cpp:370). It then logs (cpp:374) and only afterwards zeroes the count (cpp:378) and frees the slot (cpp:380). If the sealing process is killed between the CAS and cpp:378, for example during attach while it logs, the slot stays (~0, n). No discount looks at it: the namespace test at cpp:360 compares 0xffffffff, which is no process's namespace. Pass 0 and pass 1 never take it (cpp:322-330). So n stays in every poll's sum for the segment's life: SEAL_DEAD at the next attempt, and every later attempt returns at once. This is the permanent no-copy that D8's discount exists to remove, made by a dead sealer. Precondition: the sealer dies in a window of a few stores plus one log call, only while it discounts.

findings.title: An owner that execs an image without the agent stays 'alive' (same pid and start time): its device copy is gone, and no process can take the map over while that image runs

O keeps its pid and start time, and its tasks are running, so every other agent's claim() returns not_owner. If the new image loads the agent, it takes over itself (owner == self, no cached copy). If not, the mirror stays frozen, deliveries stop, and GPU probes in other processes have no copy until the exec'd image exits. Liveness of the process is not liveness of the owner's copy. Precondition: an owner process that execs (and drops the agent).

findings.problem: R is the owner giving the claim back. It CASes OWNER R->0 (cpp:503), then stores owner_start_for = 0 and owner_start = 0. Z is a claimant whose CAS 0->Z (cpp:483) follows R's CAS, and whose stores (cpp:488, 491) may interleave with R's two trailing stores. Once Z is gone and any long-lived process reuses its pid, every agent gets not_owner while that process runs: the map has an owner nobody can replace.
